children: Jazeera Airways has launched direct flights between Kuwait and Addis Ababa, marking the Kuwaiti low-cost carrier’s newest destination in Africa and strengthening air connectivity between the two countries.
The inaugural service was celebrated at Jazeera Terminal 5 with a ceremony attended by Ethiopian Ambassador to Kuwait Dr Sied Jibril and Jazeera executives.
The airline will operate three weekly flights, providing greater travel convenience for more than 70,000 Ethiopian nationals living in Kuwait.

Jibril said: “Today’s inaugural flight represents an important new chapter in the longstanding relationship between Ethiopia and Kuwait. Direct air connectivity plays a vital role in bringing countries and communities closer together, and we welcome Jazeera Airways’ new service to Addis Ababa. We believe this route will contribute to stronger tourism, trade, investment and cultural exchange, while making travel more convenient for the large Ethiopian community in Kuwait. We look forward to seeing this connection grow and create new opportunities for both countries.”

Paul Carroll, Chief Commercial Officer, Jazeera Airways, said: “Addis Ababa is an important addition to our growing network as the first and one of the most strategic destinations in Eastern Africa. This new route serves the large Ethiopian community in Kuwait and supports growing business, trade and leisure travel between the two countries. As we continue to expand, we see Africa as a significant growth market, with Addis Ababa strengthening our presence on the continent while giving passengers convenient access through Kuwait to other destinations.”

title: ZAWYA: Jazeera Airways launches direct Kuwait–Addis Ababa flights
